item.title: Rail or river rivalry? Intermodal transportation of grain through Mississippi Corridors from 2002 to 2013
item.description:
Authors: Juan Murguia, James F. Nolan, David Hennessy

Source: Research in Transportation Economics

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: U.S. grain farming occurs predominantly throughout the vast Midwest. U.S. railroads as well as barges operating on the Mississippi River have played key roles in the regional grain supply chain. While research has been done about U.S. grain transportation, surprisingly little is known about the nature and scope of intermodal competition in these freight markets. Using historical data from various sources, we estimate models of barge and railroad rates for key grain corridors and grain types. We find evidence of strong rail-barge competition in a few corridors in the region, but also uncover evidence that viable intermodal competition remains conditional on factors such as distance to shipper as well as the type of grain shipped.

Authors: Yemima Berman, Beom Hee Lee, Anthony Pak-Yin Liu, Yoshihiro Nishida, Ee Shien Tan, Zhichao Wang

Source: iScience

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a complex multisystem disorder requiring coordinated multidisciplinary care. This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations for NF1 management in the Asia-Pacific region. A modified Delphi process involving two survey rounds and a virtual meeting was conducted with experts from nine countries. A total of 141 statements were evaluated using a 9-point Likert scale with a 75% consensus threshold. Consensus was achieved across key domains including diagnosis, genetic testing, surveillance, and management. Experts emphasized the importance of multidisciplinary care, risk-adapted surveillance, and integration of genetic counseling and imaging in clinical practice. These findings provide regionally relevant guidance to support consistent and practical NF1 management across diverse healthcare systems.

item.title: The exterior Steklov problem for Euclidean domains
item.description:
Authors: Lukas Bundrock, Alexandre Girouard, Denis S. Grebenkov, Michael Levitin, Iosif Polterovich

Source: Journal of Spectral Theory

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: We investigate the Steklov eigenvalue problem in an exterior Euclidean domain. First, we present several formulations of this problem and establish the equivalences between them. Next, we examine various properties of the exterior Steklov eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. One of our main findings is an Escobar-type lower bound for the first exterior Steklov eigenvalue on convex domains in dimensions three and higher. This bound is expressed in terms of the principal curvatures of the boundary and is sharp, with equality attained for a ball. Moreover, it implies the existence of a sequence of convex domains with fixed volume and the first exterior Steklov eigenvalues tending to infinity. This contrasts with the interior case, as well as with the two-dimensional exterior case, for which we show that an analogue of the Weinstock isoperimetric inequality holds.

Abstract: Catecholamines, particularly the hormone and neurotransmitter epinephrine, are important regulators of blood pressure and cardiovascular function.
